This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 19.11.2022 at about 12.30 p.m. he had been riding his motor cycle TVS XL bearing Reg.No. KA42U2013 near Kodandarama House,
Hebbidarumettilu Road, Jakkasandra Village, Maralavadi Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42J5586 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against his motor cycle, due to the said accident he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to CDSIMER, Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as indoor patient and spent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/.
3.

At the time of the accident, he was aged about 54 years, hale and healthy, working as agriculturist and milk vendor, thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m., due to SCCH5 this accident he has lost his income and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.369/2022 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42J5586 before Harohalli police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has appeared, but not filed written statement.
R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner and submitted that,
petitioner

being the rider of the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA42U2013 riding the motor cycle without driving license, without competent to ride the said vehicle, rode in rash and negligently and hit SCCH5 to insured vehicle
, he has issued policy bearing No.14152222240000259 in respect to vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA42J5586 valid since 18.01.2022 to 17.02.2023.
The rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
Kariyappa vs Ravi Kumar .C.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2368295/
2

1. Whether Petitioner proves that, on 19.11.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. when petitioner was riding his motor cycle TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA42U2013 near Kodandarama House, Hebbidarumettilu Rasthe, SCCH5 Jakkasandra Village,
Maralavadi, Kanakapura, Ramanagara District, at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KJA42J5586 driven by its driver in a rash and negligently dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 1 witness as PW2 and marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, counsels for respondents submitted that, they have no defence evidence.
SCCH5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :
As per final order for the  following:
: : REASONS

: : 
8. Issue No.1: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is SCCH5 marked as Ex.P.4, copy of wound certificate is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.8.

9 . In crossexamination there is no dispute about place, date and time of the accident, only defence is that very accident is occurred due to negligency of the petitioner, but said such suggestion is denied by the petitioner.
R1/owner has not at all crossexamined the PW1.
Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the Ravikumar, who is rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42J5586 and caused the accident.

In support of the Kariyappa vs Ravi Kumar .C.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2368295/
3 same there are medial records such as wound certificate and discharge summary as per Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.9.
it goes to show that, out of the said accident SCCH5 petitioner has sustained injuries and taken treatment.
Considering the same, this court comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the alleged accident.
Hence, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
10. Issue No.2:

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained type I open (compound)
fracture of 3rd, 4th & 5th metacarpal of right hand, for which he undergone CRIF with 'K' wires.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.19 issued by CDSIMER, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 19.11.2022 to 25.11.2022.
11. Further Dr.Ramachandra, Senior Consultant and DNB at General Hospital is examined as PW2 and furnished OPD slip marked as Ex.P.14, Xray Films SCCH5 marked as Ex.P.15.
He has assessed permanent residual physical disability at the rate of 8% to the whole body.

12. In crossexamination admits that, he has not treated the petitioner, petitioner sustained injuries to the 3rd, 4th and 5th metacarpal bones, fractures are united, but 3rd metacarpal bone is malunion.

Further admits that, he has not expressed his opinion about mal union, further admits that, Xray Films marked at Ex.P.14 does not supported with radiology report, range of movements of fingers is not mentioned in his opinion.
Further admits that, they are non weight bearing bones, but which needs daytoday activities.
In this regard there is no observation in affidavit.
He has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
Further admits that, in discharge summary there is no entry about malunion.
Further admits that, except his clinical SCCH5 observation there is no document on record to show that mal union of 3rd metacarpal bone.
13. Petitioner is not a diabetic, there is no loss of grip and pich strength.

Further denied that,
assessment made by him is higher side, further admits that, there is no supportive documents to show that prehension, sensation and loss of strength.
Further denied that, assessment made by him is higher side.
As per the police reports, there is a grievous injury to the metacarpal bones, hence charge sheet is for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
As per the wound certificate, there is injury to 3 rd, 4th and 5th metacarpal bones, which can be corrected by way of surgery.
Further as per the discharge summary also all 3rd, 4th and 5th metacarpal bones are fractured, further he has sustained right hand injury, unable to lift and move hands.
SCCH5 14.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence.
Furthermore petitioner is age about 54 years and he is a agriculturist.

On the other hand, counsel for R2 much argued that, there is no disability,
falsely disability is assessed to help the petitioner only medical bill may be awarded.
15.

On going through the same, it is noticed that, surgery is successful and there is no pain, fracture is united, furthermore 3rd, 4th and 5th metacarpal bones are non weight bearing bones, they will not cause any inconvenience for agriculture work.

The non treated Doctor Dr.Ramachandra has assessed the permanent disability to the whole body at the rate of 8%, but considering the nature of Kariyappa vs Ravi Kumar .C.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2368295/
4

the injury, nature of the work, union of the fracture, age of the petitioner, functional disability to the whole body is considered at the rate of SCCH5 5%, which will be taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

16. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 54 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 1968 and alleged accident is occurred in 2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 his age is considered about 55 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 11 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

17. As per his case, he was working as agriculturist and milk vendor, thereby earning Rs.30,000/
p.m., to prove the said fact, he has furnished certificate issued by Yadavanahalli Milk SCCH5 Producers Cooperative Society Ltd., marked as Ex.P.13, but he has not examined the author of the document.

entities.text: Yadavanahalli Milk SCCH5 Producers Cooperative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further not furnished daily dairy maintained by him about supply of the milk.
Further in support of the same there is no bank pass book or payment receipts.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very document is not helpful to the case of the petitioner to prove his income.

On the basis of stray letter issued by the Yadavanahalli Milk Dairy, it is not possible to consider the income of the petitioner at the rate of Rs.18,000/ p.m. looking to all other attending circumstances his age, and work, this tribunal has relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 2022 23.
In the case on hand, petitioner is agricutlurist and milk vendor, so that, he comes under the category of formerly groupIV - now unskilled worker category.

Very SCCH5 accident is occurred on 19.11.2022, accordingly as on the date of accident including dearness allowances for unskilled workers minimum wages for a month will come to Rs.13,821/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, SCCH5 nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded,
for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.13,821/ towards loss of income during laid up period.

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.10 for an amount of Rs.2,647/.
19.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.

Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 13,82100 period Total 1,52,68700 SCCH5 20.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,52,687/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.141522222240000259 which is valid for the period from 18.01.2022 to 17.01.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 19.11.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further rider of the offending motor cycle by name Ravikumar C.C. had valid driving license as on the date of accident, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

SCCH5 22. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,52,687/ (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Two Thousand Six Hundred Eighty Seven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.

6 SCCH5
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
